title: Nebula Metrics — Dedicated Capacity Discovery
summary: Initial technical discovery focused on reserved GPU capacity, tenant isolation patterns, and burst/fallback behavior. Customer is leaning toward Dedicated but wants clarity on pre-warm behavior, isolation guarantees, and security controls. Agreed to run a short POC with load profiles to validate p99 latency at target throughput.
action_items: Redwood (Maya): Share Dedicated pricing worksheet and committed tier options — due 2027-04-28
Redwood (Roberto): Circulate architecture diagram (reserved pools, warm/hot pool, fallback routing) + security pack — due 2027-04-27
Customer (Evan): Provide sample prompt distribution and 7-day traffic histogram to size prewarm — due 2027-05-02
Customer (Priya): Send compliance checklist items (data residency, KMS, audit retention) — due 2027-04-30
Schedule: SE-led POC load run (2 weeks) to validate 50 rps steady, 200 rps spikes — target start 2027-05-05
next_steps: Schedule technical POC and baseline benchmark
Follow up meeting to review POC results and contract term options
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-04-25 16:00 UTC; Duration: ~52m; Attendees: Maya Chen, Roberto Diaz, Leah O'Connor / Sofia Patel, Evan Morales, Priya Sharma, Jordan Lee

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining — apologies for the slight delay, we had a calendar issue, um quick intros?
[00:08] Sofia (Nebula Metrics - CTO): hi i'm sofia, cto at nebula metrics, we do high-frequency anomaly detection for streaming sensor data. Evan will tee up ops details.
[00:15] Evan (Head of MLOps): hey all, evan here — curious about dedicated reserved GPU options and how you handle spikes.
[00:21] Maya: perfect, that's what we're here for. Roberto from our SE team will walk the performance and architecture details — roberto?
[00:27] Roberto (Redwood SE): yep thanks maya. Quick agenda: sizing for reserved capacity, isolation (tenant fencing), warm-pools and burst behavior, and the fallback to hosted variants. Also security controls — i know priya had a note on KMS and audit logs.
[00:40] Priya (Security): yes thanks, key things for us are tenant isolation guarantees, where keys live, SSO/SAML flow, and audit log retention window. Also, can you support customer-managed KMS?
[00:50] Roberto: short answer: yes on customer-managed KMS in Dedicated and Private; we'll share the exact KMS/HSM integration docs. Audit logs are plumbed to your retention store in Private; for Dedicated we can push logs to your Cloud Logging or SIEM via our log forwarder.
[01:05] Jordan (TPM): can you define "Dedicated" for us — is it single-tenant hardware or logical isolation on shared nodes?
[01:12] Maya: good q. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for your account — physical isolation can be offered depending on contract tier. For most customers we provide node-level isolation where tenants are the only ones scheduled on those GPUs; we also offer additional segregation for compliance-sensitive orgs.
[01:25] Sofia: so if we hit a sudden surge, how does Redwood handle it? do you overprovision or do we fall back to hosted models? we need predictable latency.
[01:34] Roberto: two levers: warm/hot pool pre-warmed instances and cross-tier fallback. Typical pattern: reserve a baseline pool sized for steady-state qps. We maintain a warm pool to pre-load KV cache and model weights; that covers short bursts. For larger sustained bursts we can auto-burst into a shared overflow pool (hosted) or into a reserved burst pool if you purchase burst capacity.
[01:55] Evan: what's the cold-start time to spin a GPU and get KV cache warm? we care about p95/p99 for short requests (seq len ~128 tokens).
[02:02] Roberto: cold boot of a GPU node ~2-3 minutes; warm-pool prewarmed nodes ready in <10s for model weights, but the KV cache warming depends on your prefix and prompt distribution. If you have consistent prompts we can warm common prefixes proactively. Worst-case p99 for cold-run is in the 2-3 minute class but with warm pool p99 is typically sub-300ms for a 128 token model on an A100-class node for a single request — ymmv by model size and quantization.
[02:30] Speaker 3 (mislabeled): uh, sorry can i ask about sequential batching?
[02:34] Roberto: yeah batching is automatic; we do continuous batching with latency SLOs so small requests get batched up to some degree unless you opt into strict low-latency mode which reduces batching and raises cost.
[02:45] Priya: and encryption in transit and at rest? we need AES256 at rest and TLS1.3 in flight, and kms integration.
[02:52] Maya: that's standard. For Dedicated you can bring your KMS keys; we encrypt the model cache and persisted artifacts using your keys where supported.
[03:00] Evan: example numbers: our steady load ~50 rps with spikes to 200 rps for 2-4 minutes every hour during uploads. What's a recommended reserve?
[03:09] Roberto: quick rule of thumb: assuming your model does ~0.08s per token at inference layer and average 40 tokens per request, that's ~3.2s compute per request — wait, that feels high, lemme reframe. If model latency is 200ms per request (seq len 128, quantized), then an instance can do ~5 rps, so 50 rps needs ~10 instances. But GPU throughput varies by model + batch behavior. We should size off your sample prompts; can you send the token histogram?
[03:36] Evan: yes we'll send the distribution.
[03:39] Sofia: is there an auto-scaling policy for Dedicated? we can't have noisy neighbor impact but also want cost control.
[03:45] Roberto: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling with min/max caps, cold-start protections (delay until warm pool exists), and burst ceilings that force fallbacks to hosted if exceeded. You can set rules by latency SLO or by queue depth.
[03:58] Jordan: what about routing — if scheduled jobs go to hosted fallback, how do you maintain data isolation? we have sensitive PII in some payloads.
[04:06] Maya: good. For sensitive traffic you can mark routes as "never fallback"; those will reject beyond capacity. Alternatively, Private deployment is recommended if you can't accept any egress to shared infrastructure. For Dedicated we can restrict fallback to dedicated overflow pools only — no shared tenancy — as a contract option.
[04:24] Priya: that fits. What's your SOC2 status and can you provide an ISO attestation?
[04:29] Leah (CSM): we're SOC2 Type II; we have ISO 27001 in progress — we'll attach the certs and SOC2 report in the security pack.
[04:36] Sofia: timelines: we'd like to pilot this in the next 2 weeks to validate latency under our load. Can Redwood do a 2-week POC with a testing harness?
[04:44] Roberto: yes we can spin a POC — typical run: seed your sample prompts, run load patterns (steady 50 rps with 200 rps spikes), capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost. We'll need your sample data and an API key for the POC sandbox.
[04:58] Evan: about cost: we want committed reserved pricing but with burst allowances. what's typical contract flexibility?
[05:04] Maya: committed tiers with monthly or annual terms. Burst buckets can be added as an add-on; pricing depends on reservation level — we'll send the worksheet. For negotiations we can show TCO comparisons vs your on-prem estimate.
[05:16] Speaker 2 (mislabeled): can you talk about model pinning and model variants?
[05:19] Roberto: yes model pinning supported — you can pin model versions to routes; we also offer quantized variants used automatically for cost-saving: e.g., 8-bit quantized for lower latency and lower cost with a small quality tradeoff. We can register a rollout policy so traffic shifts gradually.
[05:35] Sofia: how do you handle KV cache reuse across requests? our prompts often share large prefixes.
[05:40] Roberto: KV cache is keyed by model + prefix signature; with a warm pool we precompute common prefixes. If your prefix patterns are stable we can get a big reduction in per-token compute. We'll want sample prompts to configure that.
[05:52] Priya: audit logs — can we get token-level traces or just request metadata? we need to reconstruct actions for compliance audits.
[05:59] Leah: we capture request/response metadata and traces; response body capture is configurable due to privacy — for PII we'd advise redaction. Full token-level logs can be enabled to your log sink on Private deployments.
[06:12] Jordan: fallback SLAs — if fallback to hosted occurs, do you provide an objective warning or circuit-breaker? we need observability to fail our upstream gracefully.
[06:19] Roberto: yes, the runtime exposes events: warm pool depletion, fallback active, queue depth, p99 breaches; these surface in the Console with webhooks for incidents. You can circuit-break or route to degraded functionality.
[06:32] Sofia: ok can you walk through a hypothetical sizing with our numbers?
[06:36] Roberto: sure — with your 50 rps baseline and 200 rps peaks of 3 minutes every hour, i'd recommend a baseline reserved pool to cover 60-70 rps to be safe, then a warm pool sized for an additional 80-100 rps for short bursts. Contract add-on for a reserved burst pool if you need predictable capacity for sustained spikes; otherwise fall back to overflow with SLAs. We'll do accurate sizing once we get your token histogram.
[07:05] Evan: curious about pre-warm costs — are warm-pool nodes billed like regular reserved nodes?
[07:10] Maya: warm pool capacity is billed as reserved if allocated; we can offer cheaper warm instances (preloaded but lower compute priority) or a metered warm pool in some packages. We'll include cost tradeoffs in the pricing sheet.
[07:21] Sofia: latency targets: we need p99 < 750ms for core flows, p50 < 150ms. Do you think that's achievable?
[07:29] Roberto: for quantized models on A100/GPU equivalents and with warm pool and prefix caching, p99 under 750ms is reachable for 128 token sequences. We'll validate in POC.
[07:40] Priya: what's your incident telemetry retention? we need 365 days of audit events.
[07:45] Leah: we can retain logs for 365 days on Dedicated with premium telemetry add-on; default is 90 days. We'll include retention options.
[07:55] Jordan: network egress — do you allow VPC peering for Dedicated or is Private required?
[08:01] Maya: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private links, but Private is recommended for full air-gapped or on-prem needs. Dedicated with VPC peering still routes through our control plane.
[08:12] Sofia: any gotchas around model updates and rollouts? we can't have regressions hitting prod.
[08:16] Roberto: Console supports canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback if quality metrics degrade. You can pin write paths to the previous version during rollout. We also support automated eval hooks against your prompt set.
[08:28] Evan: who's the SE contact for the POC?
[08:30] Maya: roberto will own the POC; i'll coordinate commercial. Leah will handle CS.
[08:34] Sofia: great. for the POC, we'll need an integration window — do you do dedicated infra in our cloud region?
[08:41] Roberto: yes we support major regions; if you need a specific provider/region we'll send region availability.
[08:48] Priya: last q: do you support customer-managed keys that rotate monthly and do you expose key usage logs?
[08:55] Roberto: yes key rotation supported; usage logs can be forwarded to your KMS audit trail depending on the provider. We'll include specifics per KMS in the pack.
[09:05] Maya: ok let's recap quickly — action items and POC start date target; roberto will send architecture and schedule; maya will send pricing; customer will send prompts and compliance list. Any blockers?
[09:18] Sofia: none for now, just need the pricing to get internal approval.
[09:22] Evan: we'll prepare the traffic histograms and sample prompts.
[09:25] Priya: i'll compile the compliance checklist and forward.
[09:29] Maya: awesome. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the POC kickoff and share the docs. thanks everyone.
[09:35] End transcript (phrasing and transcription may contain minor errors: e.g., "prewarm" vs "pre-warm", some speaker labels auto-assigned).
